description:
The Pummeling Practice is a deceptively simple grappling game that reconnects men to their bodies, their presence, and each other.

Taught by @michael__gay and Connor Beaton from @mantalks at a men’s retreat, this practice invites non-verbal connection, laughter, and a return to the primal, playful energy so many of us are missing.

Whether you’re a father and son, two brothers, or just close friends—this 5-minute exercise gets you out of your head and into your body, where real trust and connection can form.

💥This isn’t about winning. It’s about being with one another.

Try it for yourself. Get all the steps on the @LiveThePractice Youtube channel.
transcript: practice is called pummeling. There's something about men sharing a non-verbal space with each other that's extremely connective. And this is a direct way to practice more of that. Something about grappling like this that just reminds us of play. You know, being in relationship with another man, testing the limits, testing our edge, testing our bodies, and doing that with another guy can just be liberating. So basically, we're just going to be chest to chest like this, hand on his back, hand on his elbow right here. And the goal is for me to try to get both hands up under where I could give a takedown here. And so we're fighting for that dominant position. And the way that we do that is we're going to try to swim our hands in and do it at the same time we'll end up back in a neutral position and i'm trying to defend while he's doing that by holding my arm close to his chest and putting my other arm my right arm down underneath so i'm trying to get double under, and he's trying to do the same thing. Human beings are wired for touch. Men get touched and have touched so little because of social constructs and mores and norms. And it deeply does something to us to not have that. And when we have an outlet where it's acceptable, it's relational, it's playful, it opens us back up to flow, vitality, ease.
